metaData.originalTitle: 阿里李飞飞首秀：一口气面向 Agent 发了 32 个新品
metaData.title: Alibaba's Li Feifei Debut: 32 New Products for Agents in One Go
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: At the 2026 Alibaba Cloud Summit, Alibaba Cloud announced a full-stack Agentic upgrade, releasing over 50 new products including the self-developed chip Zhenwu M890, flagship model Qwen3.7-Max, Agentic Cloud infrastructure, and the new AI product Qianwen Cloud, marking a shift from human-oriented to Agent-oriented cloud services.
metaData.summary: This article provides a detailed report on the 2026 Alibaba Cloud Summit, the most signal-dense press conference in Alibaba Cloud's 17-year history. Alibaba Cloud announced the completion of a full-stack Agentic upgrade from chips to inference. Key releases include: T-Head's new generation training-inference integrated AI chip Zhenwu M890 (3x performance of its predecessor) and the Panjiu AL128 supernode server; Alibaba Cloud CTO Li Feifei's release of 32 Agentic Cloud new products covering six major capabilities: runtime, orchestration, governance, security, memory, and data plane, with cloud products undergoing Skillification, MCPification, and CLIfication; the flagship model Qwen3.7-Max topping the Arena rankings domestically and autonomously working for 35 hours on the Zhenwu M890 chip to complete kernel optimization; the Bailian platform opening access to over 150 models; and the launch of the new AI product Qianwen Cloud's official website, replacing traditional navigation with a single line of instruction. The article argues that when the primary consumers of the cloud shift from humans to Agents, all interfaces and interaction logic designed for humans will be rewritten, and Alibaba Cloud is engaging in a full-stack AI race with global cloud giants like Google and Amazon.

mainPoints.point: Alibaba Cloud completes a full-stack Agentic upgrade from chips to inference, releasing over 50 new products.
mainPoints.explanation: The releases cover the self-developed AI chip Zhenwu M890, Agentic Cloud infrastructure (32 new products), the flagship model Qwen3.7-Max, the Bailian inference platform, and the new AI product Qianwen Cloud, forming a complete closed-loop technology stack.

mainPoints.point: Cloud products shift from human-oriented design to Agent-oriented design, undergoing Skillification, MCPification, and CLIfication.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional cloud product consoles and APIs are designed for humans; Agents require structured capability descriptions and clear invocation protocols. Alibaba Cloud is transforming cloud products into standardized capability modules callable by Agents, turning the cloud from a human tool into an Agent operating system.

mainPoints.point: Qwen3.7-Max autonomously works for 35 hours on the Zhenwu M890 chip to complete kernel optimization, achieving a 10x performance improvement.
mainPoints.explanation: This case demonstrates the model's ability to autonomously complete complex engineering tasks, independently performing 432 kernel evaluations and 1,158 tool calls from scratch, reflecting a paradigm shift from aligning with human preferences to aligning with task objectives.

mainPoints.point: Alibaba Cloud adopts an open ecosystem strategy, with the Bailian platform integrating over 150 models and all Qianwen Cloud Skills and CLI open-sourced.
mainPoints.explanation: Given the belief that no single model can dominate everything in the Agent era, Alibaba Cloud builds a differentiated competitive advantage by opening access to third-party models like Zhipu, MiniMax, and Kimi, as well as open-sourcing core tools.

keyQuotes: Once Agents pass the critical tipping point, they can work 24/7 without interruption, creating an insatiable demand for AI and cloud resources.

Large models are undergoing a core paradigm shift—from aligning with human preferences to aligning with task objectives. In the past, we pursued models that 'speak well'; now, we require models that 'get things done.'
Alibaba Cloud is not just adding an Agent interface layer on top of the cloud; it is transforming the cloud itself into something Agents can use.
When the primary consumers of the cloud shift from humans to Agents, all interfaces, processes, and interaction logic designed for humans will be rewritten.
